    Lines carried by a module #

    A module line in a finite set S of points of the cover is a line without extra arrows (OLine) inside S, with a representation X of the piece of S that respects the cover, whose arrows act by nonzero maps only between points of the line, and whose paths along the line act by nonzero maps (MLine). It need not be convex. If S is convex, its good pairs are rigid (MLine.rigid): a path with the value of a segment of the line has a partner in S with the same action on X (exists_partner), so it runs along the line, and paths along the line with the same ends are equal (OLine.path_unique). So a module line with 3 dim k(P) arrows gives a band (exists_lineBandRel).
